analysis: Both units are CHANGELOG.md documentation changes (head_text excerpts, lines 422+ and 616+). No executable code, config, or trust-policy source was supplied. The entries describe App Attest dead-key rotation (rate limits 1/hour and 4/24h, never revoking or denying serving, rebuilding via full attestation/receipt/qualification/assertion checks), invalidKey enrollment backoff, APNs code-identity retry, optional untrusted diagnostics on ready replies (consistent with the TB-002 untrusted-diagnostic language), public model-demand aggregates with k-anonymity suppression (20 requests / 3 accounts), and the 0.9.x release notes. These statements are consistent with the canonical TB-002/TB-009/TB-011 and T-052..T-058 model: diagnostics don't affect authorization; rotation requires fresh full verification. Nothing in the text asserts a trust-policy loosening that contradicts the threat model. Behavioral claims cannot be verified because the implementing source files were not supplied (coverage limit): the rotation admission logic, the model-demand suppression, and the admin /app-attest/diagnostics endpoint should be checked in a code pass for the claims (e.g., rotation not bypassing revocation or build-qualification gates, suppression preventing subtraction recovery, no identifiers in metric tags). The threat model may warrant an update for the new public model-demand aggregate surface (small-cohort privacy) and key-rotation as a credential continuity mechanism (T-055), but this is changelog-only evidence, so no finding is raised.
